test.title: Who owns a photograph of a building?

paragraphs.text: In some countries anyone may photograph a building from the street and sell the picture. In others the architect keeps a right over images of the work, and a magazine must ask before printing one.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The difference causes trouble online. A photograph that is legal in one country appears on a site that is read everywhere, and volunteers who write encyclopaedias have to check the law for each building.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Photographers argue that a building in a public street is part of daily life and cannot be private. Architects reply that a design takes years and is copied in seconds.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Some countries have found a middle way: pictures may be used freely if the building is not the main subject, or if the picture is not sold.
paragraphs.label: D
